description: TCP PAWS silent SYN drop through NAT with tcp_tw_reuse
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
A server has:
  net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1
  net.ipv4.tcp_timestamps = 1

It serves clients through a NAT device that maps many internal machines to a
single public IP. Client A connects (public source port 54321 → server port 443),
exchanges data, then closes normally. The server socket enters TIME_WAIT.

Within 1 second, Client B — a different physical machine behind the same NAT —
happens to be assigned source port 54321 by the NAT, and attempts a new connection
to the same server port.

Client B's SYN is silently dropped. Client B sees no RST — only a timeout after
retransmits are exhausted.

(a) Name the exact kernel mechanism responsible for dropping the SYN and state
    its decision rule precisely, including what value is compared to what.
(b) Explain why NAT breaks the invariant this mechanism depends on.
(c) State the correct fix, identifying which layer it must be applied at and why
    a server-side-only fix cannot be made safe.
